Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for India's response with the bat. Out walk the umpires and players. The players of New Zealand spread out to take their fielding positions. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma are the two openers for India. Matt Henry has the new ball and is raring to go. Samson to face. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

So 154 it is for India to chase and seal the series. Two of the three completed matches at Guwahati have been won by the side batting second. And given how lethal the Indian batting unit has looked in this series, they would feel it is their game to lose. New Zealand, meanwhile, never quite found their rhythm with the bat and will now need a full-throttle effort with the ball if they are to keep the series alive. Sanju Samson has been hunting for runs, and this shapes up as a golden opportunity to lock down the opening spot with Ishan Kishan breathing down his neck at number 3. Back in a bit with the run chase.

Glenn Phillips, the man in red-hot form, and Mark Chapman sparked a brave fightback with a 52-run stand. But once Ravi Bishnoi broke that partnership, New Zealand struggled to stitch anything meaningful together as India kept striking at regular intervals. From a relatively steady 86/3, they slipped to 112/6, with India firmly in control of the contest, blowing away the middle order of the Kiwis. It was only through Santner's timely breezy knock of 27 off 17 in the backend that pushed the total past 150.

New Zealand couldn't have gotten off to a worse possible start as they lost the top three inside the Powerplay itself. Conway yet again failed to impress, falling prey to Harshit Rana for the fifth time on this tour, while Seifert was undone by an absolute corker of a delivery produced by Bumrah upon his return in the side. At 34/3, with the cream of their batting already in the hut, New Zealand were dented badly, pushed for a reset and rebuild from scratch.

A very clinical bowling effort from India. They just didn't allow the Kiwis any freedom and effectively prevented them from forming any meaningful partnership. Barring Phillips and Chapman, no batter from the top five could cross 20 runs. Jasprit Bumrah and Ravi Bishnoi, the two incoming faces in the XI for this game, made the biggest impact tonight, both keeping things tight and conceding at under a run a ball. While Bumrah finished with 3/17 in four overs, Bishnoi was equally miserly with figures of 2/18.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going in Guwahati. Suryakumar Yadav has his men in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse and take their respective places in the field. They are followed by the two Kiwi openers, Tim Seifert and Devon Conway. Harshit Rana will get things going with the ball. Harshit to Conway. Devon has been dismissed by Rana all 4 times they have come up against each other across formats in this series. A slip in place. Here we go!

India (Playing XI) - Sanju Samson (WK), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Rinku Singh, Hardik Pandya, Shivam Dube, Harshit Rana, Ravi Bishnoi (In for Varun Chakaravarthy), Kuldeep Yadav, and Jasprit Bumrah (In for Arshdeep Singh).

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Tim Seifert (WK), Rachin Ravindra, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell, Mitchell Santner (C), Kyle Jamieson (In for Zakary Foulkes), Matt Henry, Ish Sodhi, and Jacob Duffy.

The captain of New Zealand Mitchell Santner feels the pitch should be pretty good again and says they will assess how it plays before looking to put a strong score on the board. He believes the team batted really well in the previous game and admits that with the ball, they came up against a very strong opposition with plenty of firepower. Santner adds that the team takes what it can from each game and moves on quickly, especially given the nature of the schedule with different matches and venues coming in rapid succession. Informs that they have one change. Also shares that Neesham was about to play this game, but caught a stomach bug. Ends by mentioning that Zakary Foulkes makes way for Kyle Jamieson.

The captain of India Suryakumar Yadav says the wicket looks good and expects a bit of dew later in the evening, which has influenced the decision to chase. He stresses the importance of repeating the good habits from previous games, encouraging the players to enjoy themselves and trust their instincts when out in the middle, while also staying grounded. He adds that it is reassuring to have options like Shivam Dube and Hardik Pandya chipping in with the ball. Informs that Arshdeep Singh and Varun Chakaravarthy have been rested with Jasprit Bumrah and Ravi Bishnoi replacing them.

TOSS - Right. It's toss time, and both captains are in readiness for the coin flip with Simon Doull leading the proceedings. The team sheets are exchanged now. SKY has got the coin. Santner will call. Tails is the call from Santner, but it lands as a Head. INDIA WIN THE TOSS AND WILL BOWL FIRST.

PITCH REPORT - Former Indian wicketkeeper-batter Deep Dasgupta and former New Zealand pacer Simon Doull are pitchside. Deep informs that the square boundaries measure 64 metres on one side and 66 metres on the other, with the straight hit being 74 metres. At first glance, Doull feels it doesn't look like a bad pitch at all. Mentions that there is a healthy grass covering, which should help the ball come nicely onto the bat. He adds that much of that grass appears dead and brown rather than fresh. Simon observes a few cracks, though not as many as were seen in the first couple of games. At the moment, there isn't much sheen on the surface, and it is on the drier side, but both Dasgupta and Doull agree that it could change later in the evening once the dew settles in.

BlackCaps seek consistency through reinforcements! For New Zealand, reinforcements are either already in or on the way. Lockie Ferguson has joined the squad, though his availability for this series remains uncertain. With the likes of James Neesham and Finn Allen set to come in as well, experience will not be in short supply. Rachin Ravindra finding his touch again is an encouraging sign, but after Zakary Foulkes went for plenty last time out, a change in the pace attack looks likely, with Kyle Jamieson expected to get the nod. The visitors clearly have the ideas and the tools to succeed in these conditions, but consistency and sustained execution remain the missing pieces, which they would want to sort out this time around. With the series on the line and everything to play for, expect nothing but fireworks again. Toss and teams coming up next very shortly.

Batting brilliance fuels India’s charge! For India, the batting unit has flexed its muscle completely this time out. Abhishek Sharma is batting in a dream run, and India will hope that his purple patch rolls on just as it did through 2025. The first T20I was his show, the second was driven by Ishan Kishan’s scintillating assault, and capped off by Suryakumar Yadav’s breathless 82 as the Indian captain finally flipped the switch after a lean spell. And with an intimidating batting depth and options available, it looks sorted out for now. On the bowling front, Jasprit Bumrah is expected to return under the rotation policy, which could see either Harshit Rana or Arshdeep Singh make way. Axar Patel’s availability remains uncertain, but on Guwahati’s typically slowish surface, India might be tempted to persist with a three-spinner combination.

A true fighting spirit, but missing results! New Zealand, meanwhile, have shown their trademark resilience, producing spirited fightbacks and refusing to roll over, as seen in this series too. However, that grit has not consistently converted into results, with the BlackCaps still without a single T20I win against Australia, England, or India since the last T20 World Cup. They face a must-win clash, as defeat would end their series hopes.

India’s T20I dominance stays intact! India’s road towards defending their T20 World Cup title has been nothing short of authoritative. Even if results in the other formats have wobbled, the shortest format has firmly belonged to them. This is a team dictating terms and overwhelming opponents. Since 29th June 2024, after ending their ICC trophy drought, India have suffered just five defeats while racking up 30 wins in 39 T20Is, numbers that scream dominance rather than mere form. The baton passing to the young gen has been smooth and effortless.

Super Sunday Blockbuster in Guwahati! After the fireworks of runs in Nagpur and Raipur, the five-match T20I series heads further east to the picturesque state of Assam for what promises to be a thrilling and decisive 3rd T20I. A very warm welcome to everyone at the scenic Barsapara Stadium in Guwahati. India have stamped their authority on this series, leading 2-0, and will be looking to wrap it up here. The Blackcaps, meanwhile, are determined to strike back and keep their series hopes alive.
... MATCH DAY ...

Sunday Showdown! Super Sunday in Guwahati sets the stage for a potentially decisive contest as India and New Zealand lock horns in the third T20I of this five match series, with the hosts in complete control leading 2-0 and the visitors staring at a must-win situation. India's Dominance - India have dominated the series so far, winning both games convincingly and sending a strong message ahead of the World Cup. After Abhishek Sharma's explosive 84 off 35 powered India to a 48-run win in the opener, the second T20I turned into a landmark night as India pulled off a stunning chase of 209, their joint-highest successful T20I chase. It was also India's 100th T20I at home, highlighted by Ishan Kishan's 76 off 32 and a return to form for skipper Suryakumar Yadav, who sealed the game with an unbeaten 82 along with fireworks from Shivam Dube. With Hardik Pandya and Rinku Singh still to come, it once again underlined the depth and flexibility in this Indian batting unit. However, Sanju Samson has been quiet in the two games and Shreyas Iyer might come in for him as he was named in the squad for the first three matches only, with Kishan doing the keeping duties. India's bowling has complemented the batting nicely. Harshit Rana made an immediate impact yet again after coming into the side, bowling a maiden-wicket over first up and removing Devon Conway, making it four games in a row with his wicket, including three times in the ODI series. Varun Chakravarthy and Kuldeep Yadav have controlled the middle overs, while Hardik and Arshdeep Singh have chipped in with key breakthroughs. Jasprit Bumrah was rested in the last game and Axar Patel missed out due to an injury. It will be interesting to see whether they come back in the team or get some more time off to manage their workload. Do or Die for New Zealand - New Zealand, on the other hand, have struggled to find consistency despite flashes of individual brilliance. Glenn Phillips' 78 in the first game and Mitchell Santner's fiery 47 in the second were positives, while Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman have looked fluent without converting starts into big scores. Tim Seifert could be a major X-factor at the top after a strong run in the Big Bash League, and his ability to take on the Powerplay may be key. With the ball, Matt Henry remains their main weapon, while Jacob Duffy, currently ranked 4th in the world in T20Is, has been impressive with his variations. Captain Santner, along with Ish Sodhi, needs to control the middle overs to try and contain the explosive batting unit of the hosts. Zakary Foulkes had a tough outing in the last game, conceding 67 runs in 3 overs and it is highly likely Kyle Jamieson comes in for him. Jamieson will also be under pressure to deliver after replacing the injured Adam Milne in the World Cup squad, making this series a crucial opportunity for him. Probable Playing XI - India - Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan (WK), Shreyas Iyer, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Hardik Pandya, Shivam Dube, Rinku Singh, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Axar Patel, Varun Chakaravarthy. New Zealand - Tim Seifert (WK), Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell, Mitchell Santner (C), Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Ish Sodhi, Jacob Duffy. What to expect? The Barsapara Stadium in Guwahati is known for being a batter-friendly venue, with flat surfaces and quick boundaries often leading to big scores. Interestingly, India have won only once in T20Is at this ground, with their two losses coming against Australia while batting first. With the pitch once again expected to favour stroke play, another high-scoring encounter could be on the cards as India look to wrap up the series and New Zealand fight to stay alive.
